findings.summary: Regression from the F2 fix: the quote scan is no longer linear on a long text node. opensBlock() runs preg_replace() over substr($text, 0, $offset), the whole run before the mark, for every opening single mark in running text with no quotation open, so a run with m such marks costs O(m × length), and the pattern’s repeated group backtracks through every whitespace run besides. At 6598ce5 a dialogue paragraph 4× as long takes 4.0× as long; at e574efb it takes 14.9×. A 60 KB paragraph of single-quoted dialogue goes from 10 ms to 427 ms, a 100 KB pretty-printed (indented) one from 10 ms to 2.4 s, a 250 KB one from 51 ms to 7.1 s and a 500 KB one (half the default maxPageBytes) from 93 ms to 28.3 s, which is past PHP’s default max_execution_time, an uncatchable fatal, against README:141 (“It never breaks a page”). Text mode (the filter on a plain-text field) is the same: 14.3×. The engine’s own perf guards promise this property (tests/engine/unit.php:443, “The quote scan is linear on a long text node”) but their possessive paragraph has one opening mark, so none of them reaches the new call. The realistic 100 KB perf page is unaffected (median 5.08 ms against 5.06 ms on the dense page), because its paragraphs are short.
